objective: Add the one-way adapter that binds a captured ROS 2 runtime TaskEvent to a Workbench action_result as execution evidence rather than a completion claim, so a runtime task and a product-side run share one correlation identity instead of being matched by timestamp.
decision_supported: Whether a runtime task can share one correlation identity with a Workbench run, and whether a product-side consumer can read a runtime terminal event as execution evidence without treating it as proof that an actuator moved.
acceptance: A captured ROS 2 runtime TaskEvent binds to a Workbench run and action_result derived from the runtime's own request_id, workflow_id and task_id, with the ROS 2 goal_id as the action_id, and re-delivery of the same line replays instead of writing a second result

A TaskEvent never produces a verification result and never claims a physical action: a non-success terminal outcome maps to a non-confirmed device_state, and the completion decision stays with the World Model verifier
The adapter writes no spatial claim, because the runtime reports the device it commanded and never where the entity ended up, and a guessed entity would mislead every later verifier
A record missing a correlation field, carrying an unknown status or outcome, an out-of-range code, or an unreadable stamp is refused rather than written, and the refusal names the failing line
ROS 2 stays out of the Workbench dependency set: the transport is a captured JSONL file, not a DDS subscription
evidence: tests/integration/test_ros2_runtime_task_events.py drives a completed event, three non-success terminal outcomes, ten unusable records, a replayed retry, a restart replay, and a capture whose failing line is reported
the task packet changed-path validation output and the contract gate output
the full unit and integration suite result recorded on this commit
stop_conditions: stop if the runtime adapter would have to subscribe to DDS to be useful, because ROS 2 is not a Workbench dependency
stop if binding a TaskEvent would require a new WorldEventType, because action_result already carries execution evidence and a new type is an interface decision
stop if a TaskEvent can only be bound by guesswork from a timestamp, because an unbound event must be refused rather than written
stop if the adapter would need to edit interfaces/, libs/contracts/ or services/
risks_and_fallbacks: A runtime capture could be older than the correlation contract; fallback is that a missing request_id, workflow_id or goal_id is refused so an unbound event is never written by guesswork

A TaskEvent could be read as proof that the robot moved; fallback is that the adapter writes action_result only, maps a non-success outcome to a non-confirmed device_state, and leaves the completion decision to the World Model verifier

A runtime run_id could collide with a Workbench run_id; fallback is that the length-prefixed request_id/workflow_id/task_id tuple is namespaced under run: and cannot render equal to a product run identity
rollback is a revert of this commit; the change is additive, adds no dependency, and touches no schema, store, seed or runtime path
